newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA GROSS FOREIGN DEBT FALLS BY $165 MLN Q1.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA GROSS FOREIGN DEBT FALLS BY $165 MLN Q1.

text.p: Bulgaria's gross foreign debt fell by $165 million in the first quarter of this year to $9.494 billion, preliminary Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) figures showed.
"Compared to December 31 the debt was reduced by $165 million or 1.7 percent," the BNB report said.
By March 31 long-term debt fell by $225.7 million to $8.060 billion or 84.9 percent of gross foreign debt from $8.286 billion or 85.8 percent of debt at end-1996.
Short-term dues grew by 4.4 percent or $60.7 million to $1.434 billion or 15.1 percent of the total debt.
Commercial debt restructured in Bulgarian government Brady bonds stood at $4.984 billion or 56 percent of total debt in the first quarter.
Dues to multilateral lenders have fallen to $1.620 billion or 17.1 percent of total debt from $1.714 billion at the end of last year.
Debt to the Paris Club of government creditors stood at $957 million, down from $1.034 billion last year. Comparative figures for the first quarter of last year were not available.
The 1997 budget, approved on Saturday, envisages interest payments on foreign debt at 2.9 percent of projected gross domestic product for the year. GDP was projected at 16.150 trillion levs.
